plan: [ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. This ensures you win whenever it’s profitable (when your value exceeds the second-highest bid) and you pay that second-highest bid, not your own. With value $48 and $0.1 increments, bid 48. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction with i.i.d. private values (Uniform[0,49]). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding risks winning at a price above value; underbidding risks losing when you would have earned positive surplus. No useful history exists (round 1 of 1), and values are redrawn independently each round. Therefore, bid exactly my value, $38. Ties are random; shading to avoid ties is not profitable. ]

[ Second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values: truthful bidding is weakly dominant. With value 12, bidding 12 ensures we win exactly when our value exceeds competitors’ bids and we pay the second-highest bid. Overbidding risks paying above value due to tie-breaking; underbidding risks losing positive-surplus cases. No history to exploit and only 1 round, so prioritize dominant-strategy truth-telling to maximize expected profit. ]
